- The specific Firefox release version that contains this exact patch note.

- Any related Bugzilla entries or developer documentation that tie this performance improvement to a particular version and date.

3. FACTS TO DERIVE
- The likely timeframe of the release based on Windows 11 22H2’s rollout (late 2022), mapping to Firefox’s version numbers and release dates around that period.
- Whether the note applies to general performance or a specific subsystem (e.g., accessibility, URL retrieval hooks) by correlating bug descriptions and release notes summaries.
- Whether the version is a mainline release or ESR by comparing release cadence and notes content.

4. EDUCATED GUESSES
- The relevant Firefox versions likely fall around 105–107 (September–November 2022), coinciding with Windows 11 22H2’s release window.
- The note may have appeared in the standard desktop release notes rather than ESR, given the timing and the nature of performance improvements.
- The phrasing suggests either a platform-specific note or a localized note; it may be present verbatim in English release notes or as a translation from a regional page.
